messages.author: c4ad98ee09d9ee51
messages.subject: Combining Data Frames
parts:
Hi All,

I would like a graph that has two sets of data plotted together. I've
been using the 'melt' command for this and it's working fine. I'm
encountering a problem is when I try to put error bars on the data
points. When I melt my data frame the error values are included in the
same column as the data. So far I haven't been able to find any way to
create two value columns using 'melt', is there an alternative?

I've also tried calling two separate data frames which seems to
confuse R, I get an error message instead of a plot


For reference -

DF <- read.table("LightCurve.csv", header=TRUE, sep=",")
new.data<-melt(DF,id.var="X",na.rm=FALSE)

####For error bars - this is for when I try to use separate data
frames
error <- read.table("LCrror2.csv", header=TRUE, sep=",")
new.error<-melt(error,id.var="Val",na.rm=FALSE)

G <- ggplot(new.data,aes(x=X,y=-value))+
geom_point(shape = variable) +
scale_x_continuous("JD - 2450000") +
scale_y_continuous("Magnitude Difference",breaks = c(-13, -12.5, -12,
-11.5, -11), label = c("13", "12.5", "12", "11.5", "11")) +
coord_cartesian()

G + labs(shape = "Filter")

G + geom_errorbar(aes(ymax = -value - new.error, ymin = - value +
new.error))


And a sample of my original data frame -

MMO(645) AKO(645) Arror Mrror
5154 11 0.1
5156 12 0.1
5197 12 0.75
5198
5201 11 0.1
5202
5206 12 0.75
5208 13 0.15


Any help is much appreciated!

messages.author: 99a1cfc66539313c
messages.subject: Re: Combining Data Frames
parts:
Alexa

Melt will do what you need. However, there is a small semantic error
in your code. The parameter for melt() is id.vars="x". Notice that
you used id.var="x", i.e. there is an "s" missing in your code.
Because of this, melt() will use the default behaviour, which isn't
what you are looking for. I suspect if you fix this one line of code,
your original approach will work.

Andrie

That does work. The problem is that because the columns are still
labelled the same I couldn't call the error values without R getting
confused. What I ended up doing is this:

library("ggplot2")
library("reshape")

DF <- read.table("LightCurve.csv", header=TRUE, sep=",")

new.data<-melt(DF,id.vars="X",na.rm=FALSE, measure.vars=c("MMO.
645.","AKO.645."))

error2 <- error$value

G <- ggplot(new.data,aes(x=X,y=-value))+
geom_point(aes(shape = variable)) +
scale_x_continuous("JD - 2450000") +
scale_y_continuous("Magnitude Difference",breaks = c(-13, -12.5, -12,
-11.5, -11), label = c("13", "12.5", "12", "11.5", "11")) +
coord_cartesian()

Graph <- G + labs(shape = "Filter")

Graph + geom_errorbar(aes(ymax = -value - error2, ymin = - value +
error2))


Thank you for your help! I appreciate it.
